questions.question: Spongilla is an example of ______ water sponge.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__fresh.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Spongilla is a freshwater sponge.
 
• It is a member of the family Spongillidae.
 
• It is generally found in lakes, ponds, and slow streams.
 
• Sponges belong to the phylum Porifera. They are generally marine and mostly asymmetrical animals.
 
• These are primitive multicellular animals and have a cellular level of organization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum.
 
• This pathway of water transport is helpful in food gathering, respiratory exchange, and removal of waste. Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals.
 
• Digestion is intracellular. The body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres.
 
• Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite), i.e., eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual.
 
• Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation and sexually by the formation of gametes.
 
• Fertilization is internal and development is indirect having a larval stage that is morphologically distinct from the adult.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a kind of question related to Indian Parliamentary Proceedings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yearly Question**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Parliamentary Proceedings**

 
 
• The first hour of every parliamentary sitting is for **''The Question hour''.**
 
• The members ask questions and the ministers usually give answers during this time.
 
 
 
• **The questions are of three kinds**:
 
 
• **Starred question**: It requires an oral answer and hence any supplementary questions can follow.
 
• **Unstarred question**: It requires a written answer, for this reason, supplementary questions cannot follow.
 
• **Short notice question**: It is a type of question that is asked by giving a notice of fewer than ten days. It is answered orally, not require any written answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a natural pesticide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rotenone**__**.**

__
 
• **Rotenone** is an example of a **natural pesticide.**
 
• **Rotenone **is used as a **pesticide, insecticide**, and as** nonselective piscicide.**
 
• It is a naturally occurring complex ketone, derived from the roots of the Lonchocarpus species.
 
• It is a commonly used pesticide and is also used in lakes and reservoirs to kill fish that are perceived as pests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT) **is an insecticide used in agriculture. The United States banned the use of DDT in 1972. Some countries outside the United States still use DDT to control of mosquitoes that spread malaria.
 
• **Heptachlor -** It** **is used primarily against **soil insects** and **termites. **It is also used against **some crop pests** and to **combat malaria.**
 
• **Chlordane or chlordan, **is an **organochlorine compound **used as a **pesticide.** It was first used to **eradicate the termites.**

questions.question: Mudiyettu is a ritual dance drama from Kerala based on the mythological tale of a battle between the Goddess ______ and the demon Darika.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mudiyettu **__

 
 
• It is a traditional ritual theatre and folk dance drama from **Kerala. **
 
• **It enacts the mythological tale of a battle between the goddess Kali and the demon Darika. **
 
• **The ritual is a part of the Bhagavathi or Bhadra Kali cult. **
 
• It is performed in Kerala’s Bhagvati Kavus, the temples of the Mother Goddess, between February and May after the harvesting season. 
 
• **In 2010, Mudiyettu was inscribed in the UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**
 
• **It becomes the second art form in Kerala after Koodiyattam. **
 
• The characters involved in the Mudiyettu ritual are **Bhadrakali, Narada, Darika, Shiva, Daanavendra, Koyichaadar,** and **Kooli**.

questions.question: As per the data of 2017-18 released by National Horticulture Board, which of the following states is the largest producer of Tur (Arhar) in India?
questions.solution:

__

__
 
• Major pulses grown in India are tur (arhar), urad, moong, masur, peas, and gram.
 
• Being leguminous crops, all these crops except arhar help in restoring soil fertility by fixing nitrogen from the air.
 
• Gram is the most dominant pulse but only with a share of around 40 percent in the total production followed by Tur/Arhar at 15 to 20 per cent and Urad/Black Matpe and Moong at around 8-10 percent each.
 
• National Food Security Mission for Pulses, Pulses Development Scheme and Technological Mission on Pulses are a few of the government’s plans to support pulses production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Temperature: Between 20-27°C
 
• Rainfall: Around 25-60 cm.
 
• Soil Type: Sandy-loamy soil.
 
 
 
• Top Pulses Producing States: **Madhya Pradesh > Rajasthan > Maharashtra > Uttar Pradesh > Karnataka.**
 
• India is the largest producer as well as the consumer of pulses in the world.

questions.question:
Arrange the following in ascending chronological order of construction.

A: Taj Mahal

B: Konark Sun Temple

C: Golden Temple

D: Brihadeeswarar Temple
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**D, B, C, A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brihadishvara Temple**__

 __
 
• **Brihadishvara Temple is also called, Rajarajeswaram.**
 
• It is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva.
 
• It is located on the South Bank of the **Cauvery river in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India**.
 
• Rajaraja Chola, who commissioned the temple, called it Rajarajeshwaram. 
 
• **It was built in the year 1010 by King Raja Raja Chola**.
 
• This makes the temple more than 1000 years old.
 
 
 
• **The Konark Sun Temple**__
 __
 
• **The temple was built by King Narasimhadeva I in 1250 AD.**
 
• It is declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
 
• It is also called **Surya Devalaya, Black Pagoda**.
 
• It was built in the **Odisha style of architecture or Kalinga architecture**.
 
• **The Konark temple was constructed as a huge chariot of the Lord Sun, with 12 pairs of ornamented wheels pulled by seven horses**.
 
• It is also known as** ‘Black Pagoda’ **due of its dark color.
 
 
 
• **Golden Temple**__
 __
 
• One of Amritsar's greatest attractions.
 
• Its spiritual hub is the **Sri Harmandir Sahib, commonly known as the Golden Temple**. 
 
• This is the holiest temple in the Sikh faith.
 
• **Guru Ramdas Sahib, the 4th of 10 Sikh gurus, constructed the temple and its pool in the 1500s as a place of worship for all**.
 
• The temple has been renovated many times, adding features such as the marble inlays along the floor. 
 
• **Maharaja Ranjit Singh, founder of the Sikh Empire of India (1799-1849) had the temple's upper floors covered in 750 kilos of pure gold**
 
 
 
• **Taj Mahal**__
 
 
• **An immense mausoleum of white marble, built in Agra between 1631 and 1648 by order of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.** 
 
• The Taj Mahal is the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage.
 
• The Taj Mahal is **located on the right bank of the Yamuna River.**
 
• It is located in the **Agra District of Uttar Pradesh. **

questions.question: Which of the following is inscribed in the UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nowruz.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Nowruz is the **Iranian New Year**, which is widely known as the **Persian New Year** and is celebrated worldwide by some religious groups.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the first of **Farvardin – Zoroastrian calendar’s first month** and the onset of spring.
 
• Listed in **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity of India**, the festival is also known as **Navroj, Nowrouz, Navruz,Novruz, and Nevruz.**
 
• The festival commences at the vernal equinox stroke, the time when the sun passes through the equator. 
 
• It is celebrated in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, India, Iran, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. 
 
• In India, it is mostly celebrated in **Gujarat and Maharashtra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Historical Significance:**

 
• The tradition began long ago and is baptized after the Persian King, **Jamshed** who introduced the Parsi calendar. Thus, the name – Jamshed-i-Nowroz.
 
• **King Jamshed **was held on high for his **righteousness and truthfulness. **So, Parsis also celebrate the king during the festival signifying **walking on the virtuous path and living truthfully.**
 
• All over the world, the **Parsi community and various sects of Muslims (Sunni and Shia, both) celebrate Nowruz.**
 
• Parsis pray at **Atash Behram **(Fire of Victory- the highest fire grade of a fire that can be placed in a Zoroastrian fire temple as an eternal flame).

questions.question: The laws governing the Supreme Court of India and the concept of 'procedures established by law' were adopted from the Constitution of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The laws governing the Supreme Court of India and the concept of 'Procedure established by Law' were adopted from the Japanese Constitution.
 
• The “Procedure Established by Law” means that a law duly enacted by the legislature or the concerned body is valid only if the correct procedure has been followed to the letter.
 
• By adopting the phrase "procedure established by law" the Constitution gave the legislature the final word to determine the law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Some other borrowings in Indian Constitution:

 
 
 
 
 
 

 **The Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
 
• **Blueprint of the Constitution of India.**
 
 
 
 

 **British**
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary form of Government**
 
• **The idea of the rule of law**
 
• **Law-making procedure**
 
• **Office of the CAG**
 
• **Single citizenship**
 
• **Bicameralism**
 
 
 
 

 **United States**
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
• **Power of Judicial Review and Independence of Judiciary**
 
• **Written Constitution**
 
• **Preamble**
 
• **post of Vice-President**
 
 
 
 

 **Irish**
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
• **Methods of Election of the President**
 
• **Nomination of Members in the Rajya Sabha by the President**
 
 
 
 

 **Canadian**
 
 
 
• **A Quasi-Federal form of Government**
 
• **The idea of residual powers**
 
• **Appointment of State Governors by centre**
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**
 
 
 
 

 **Former USSR**
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
• **Five Year Planning**
 
 
 
 

 **Australia**
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**
 
• **Provision regarding Trade, Commerce, and Intercourse**
 
• **Languages of the Preamble**
 
• **Joint sitting in the Parliament**
 
 
 
 

 **Germany**
 
 
 
• **Suspension of Fundamental Rights during the emergency.**
 
 
 
 

 **South Africa**
 
 
 
• **Procedure of Constitutional Amendment.**
 
 
 
 

 **France**
 
 
 
• **Liberty, equality and fraternity.**

questions.question: Which of the following has the same dimension as pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stress.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stress is developed in a body** when it is **subjected to a deforming force**.
 
• An opposite and equal force develops in response to the force applied.
 
• The restoring force per unit area of a body is called **stress**. The restoring force is equal to and the opposite of the deforming force applied to the body. It can also be defined as the deforming force per unit area of the body.
 
• So it has the same dimensions as that of pressure **(force/area). **
 
• **Dimension of Pressure and Stress: **M L⁻¹ T⁻²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Strain**__** **

 __
 
• It is the **result of stress** experienced by the body.
 
• It may be observed in the **form of physical deformation** undergone by the body.
 
• It can be measured as the ratio of change in dimension to the original dimension.
 
• So it is **unitless**.
 
 
 
• **Work**__
 __
 
• It is a measure of energy expended to move an object over a certain distance.
 
• It is expressed as the **product of the force**(required to move the object) **and the displacement.**
 
• So its dimensions are **ML²T⁻²**.
 
 
 
• **Force**__** **
 
 
• In physics, a force is an influence that can change the motion of an object. 
 
• It is an external agent that results in a change in the state(rest or motion) of an object.
 
• It is expressed as the **product of mass**(of the object under change of state) **and acceleration** (of the object during the change).
 
• So its dimensions are **MLT⁻².**

questions.question: In 1924, Mahatma Gandhi got elected as the President of the Indian National Congress in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Belgaum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Belgaum Session 1924**__

 
 
• It was the **39th session **of the Indian National Congress.
 
• **It was the only session chaired by** **Mahatma Gandhi.**
 
• It is here that spinning was made the mainstay of activity and Gandhi declared Non-violent non-cooperation as a means to attain political freedom.
 
 
 
• ​ **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded in **Bombay in December 1885**.
 
• INC was founded under the leadership of Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji, W.C. Bonnerji, Surendranath Banerji, Romesh Chandra Dutt, S. Subramania Iyer.
 
• The formation of the Indian National Congress was an effort to promote the **process of nation-building**.
